newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc to consolidate in 1997, rise in 98-UBS.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc to consolidate in 1997, rise in 98-UBS.

text.p: UBS said it expected the Swiss franc to consolidate over the next six months, with the mark moving between 83.50 and 84.50 Swiss centimes.

"But in the medium term we expect the franc to firm in view of the uncertainties over the euro, which should increase again at the end of 1998 in connection with elections in Germany," it said in a research note.
UBS said it expected Swiss interest rates to remain low for the time being given the sluggish state of the economy and the lack of inflationary pressure.

"The risk of an abrupt turn in interest rates seems small in this regard, as economic growth in surrounding European countries as well is strengthening only gradually and monetary braking is not yet necessary," it said.
"In light of the historically low yield level, however, we expect nonetheless that the trend will head moderately higher toward the end of this year as well as in the course of 1998."
